cells.tense: The harvest is at the door right now, and your hands are open to it.
cells.ask: Take one thing that's arrived and actually receive it — use it, or let it change one plan you'd already made for today.
cells.core:
Something you took care of has come in bigger than you expected. Fruit, a result, a person doing well. It's landing at your door and you're not treating it as a bill.

What's yours here is a receiver, not a trophy. You let it come in, you don't grip it, you don't tally it against what it cost. On a good day the arrival gets to be just that — you say thank you and it stays on the table where you can reach it. So the offering is to take one thing that's arrived and let it land in your hand today, whatever it turns out to be.
cells.sheetLine: Growth is arriving and your hands are open for it.
cells.place: where what's been outside comes in

cells.tense: You're already at next year's harvest while this one sits unopened at the door.
cells.ask: Name one thing that's already grown and stop before you improve it, replant it, or explain it to anyone.
cells.core:
Something good is arriving and you're already past it. Planning the next crop, correcting the yield, checking whether the numbers hold. The result is here, but you're living a season ahead of it, so it hasn't landed anywhere.

On a good day you stand in the garden and let it be enough for an hour — the planning comes out of what you've already received, and there's no defending to do. This stretch, the season ahead has your attention and the present one is going unopened. So the offering is to name one thing that's grown and stop improving it, replanting it, or explaining it to anybody. Let it sit as it is.
cells.sheetLine: The growth is here and you're already planning the next one.
cells.place: where what's been outside comes in

cells.tense: Something grew and is waiting at the threshold, and you haven't walked out to meet it.
cells.ask: Go look at one thing that grew while you weren't watching — a drawer, a yard, a person — and say out loud what it actually is.
cells.core:
You kept to the old shape of the day. Some growing thing finished and arrived, and instead of walking out to where the result is, you stayed at the workbench. Stepping across isn't locked off.

On a good day you turn toward the result and let it count as one — the finished thing is finished, and you're there with it. The short part of this stretch is the receiving, not the work. So the offering is to go look at one thing that grew without your watching, and say out loud what it actually is. A drawer, a yard, a person will do.
cells.sheetLine: Something grew and is waiting, and you haven't walked out.

cells.tense: What's arriving isn't a stroke of luck — you spent a long time at the work, and you don't say so.
cells.ask: Tell one person about a thing you grew and how you did it — the hours, not just the luck, and no downplaying.
cells.core:
You've been building this without calling it building. People around you assume the good is just turning up, and you've been letting them assume it. Half the story is being told to you by other people.

On a good day you walk into the room with the results and mention the hours that went in — they're yours and you say so. This stretch, the credit is landing on circumstance instead of on the hands that made it. So the offering is to tell one person about a thing you grew and how you did it — the hours, not just the result. No downplaying it, no 'oh anyone would have.'
cells.sheetLine: The good that's arriving is the sum of your own hours.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person always chose the tending themselves — plenty arrives without anyone's hand, and the card can simply be what's coming in. A reader could say the growth wasn't theirs to begin with. The asks survive being wrong: each asks for one plain act today, nothing riding on whether the reading is right. The line that serves me more than them is 'you're the one deciding what gets passed on' — the map carries no choosing, only arriving abundance, so it stays out.
